clue.text: Recalled Mexican food consumed in the Spanish place

indicators.note: called back, so the whole assembled piece is read in the opposite direction
something consumed is taken inside, so the food goes within the Spanish article

parts.note: el is the Spanish for 'the'
a taco is a Mexican filled tortilla

explanation.surface: Someone remembers Mexican food eaten in a Spanish restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed in' gives ETACOL before 'Recalled' turns it round; LE would be French, so the article must be the Spanish EL.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to put it in position, so the verb works as a synonym of place.

clue.text: Stop using computer design with fine following

parts.note: a logo is a graphic design or emblem
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
F (as in 'p. 5f') is the abbreviation for following

explanation.surface: An instruction to quit the computer drawing program, adding a penalty afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To log off is to end a session on a computer system, ceasing to use it.

clue.text: I'm unsure after bungling count in sequence

indicators.note: the hesitation comes after the jumbled letters
bungling means making a mess of, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: um is the noise of someone hesitating or unsure

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates after making a mistake counting things in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungling' rearranges the two words to CONTIN; 'after' places the hesitation at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A continuum is an unbroken series or progression, much like a sequence.

clue.text: Property contains needless empty passage

indicators.note: contains means holds inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a trait is a property or characteristic

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its inside, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A building has a corridor that serves no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the first and last letters of 'needless'; 'contains' sets them inside the property word.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing across or through, a synonym of passage.

clue.text: German scientist's chum, bold type to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A German scientist's friend appears in heavy print.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander von Humboldt was a celebrated German naturalist and explorer.

clue.text: Dubious novice nun shaken, caught inside with diamonds

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the rearranged letters
shaken things are jumbled up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A new nun, rattled after being caught wearing diamonds, looks doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaken' rearranges NOVICE NUN; 'inside' puts C among those letters, then D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dubious about a claim is doubtful, not persuaded of it.

clue.text: Drinking spirit after vocal disapproval

indicators.note: the spirit comes after the disapproval in the answer

parts.note: boo is the noise a jeering crowd makes
zing means energy, liveliness or spirit

explanation.surface: Someone takes to drink after being jeered.
explanation.definitionFit: Boozing is informal for drinking alcohol heavily.

clue.text: Pruned parts of plants drop

indicators.note: pruned means cut back, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: leaves are parts of plants

explanation.surface: Cut-back bits of plants fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a subject or a habit is to drop it, abandon it.

clue.text: Supports team in industrial area

parts.note: tees support golf balls
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Someone backs a sports team in a factory district.
explanation.walkthrough: TEESSIDE is an industrial region of north-east England around Middlesbrough.
explanation.definitionFit: Teesside is known for steelmaking and chemical works, a classic industrial region.

clue.text: Agreeable redevelopment of Ealing

indicators.note: redeveloping a place rebuilds it differently, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasant regeneration of a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A genial person is friendly and pleasant, which is agreeable.

clue.text: Praise one keeping company with boy

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone is commended for keeping a youngster company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts COLAD inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of praise.

clue.text: Suddenly becomes free, thereby displaying underwear?

definitions.meaning: a door or gate that ... swings free all at once
flies are the fastening on trousers; if they are open the underwear shows

explanation.surface: Something bursts loose and embarrassingly exposes someone's undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly open is to burst apart suddenly; trouser flies left undone reveal what is beneath.

clue.text: Exit hospital ward with Scandinavian giving details

parts.note: to part is to depart or exit
ICU is the intensive care unit of a hospital
Lars is a common Scandinavian man's name

explanation.surface: A Nordic patient leaves intensive care and supplies information.
explanation.definitionFit: Particulars are specific facts or items of information, that is details.

clue.text: Fancies cider cask, just all the contents

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its insides, all bar the first and last letters, taken from both words

explanation.surface: Someone imagines what is in a barrel of cider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all the contents' takes IDE from cider and AS from cask.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancies in the sense of notions or thoughts are ideas.

clue.text: Having trouble catching goat, say, identified as culprit

parts.note: a goat is an example of something that butts, a butter
to finger someone is to inform on them as guilty

explanation.surface: A goat is singled out as the guilty party.
explanation.definitionFit: A butterfingered person is clumsy and keeps dropping things, poor at catching.

clue.text: Diverts walker from south around city

indicators.note: the reversed walker goes around the city letters
in a down clue, reading from the south means going upwards, backwards

parts.note: a strider is someone walking with long steps
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A hiker coming up from the south takes a detour round a town.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'from south' means read upwards, giving REDIRTS; 'around' wraps that round the City of London postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: To redirect is to send something on another route, so it diverts.

clue.text: King in section of Observer article is island native

indicators.note: the king is placed in between the other two pieces

parts.note: the iris is part of the eye, an observer's organ
an is the indefinite article
HM stands for His Majesty

explanation.surface: A monarch appears in part of a newspaper article about an islander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observer' looks like the Sunday newspaper, but it is the eye; 'in' splits the eye part and the article to seat the king.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irishman is a native of Ireland, an island.

clue.text: Richard Curtis film, perhaps, showing city commander troubled about love

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the zero
troubled means disturbed, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A film by Richard Curtis shows a city's leader worried about romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges CITY COMMANDER; 'about' puts those letters round O. Richard Curtis wrote Four Weddings and a Funeral and Notting Hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtis's films are light-hearted love stories, examples of the romcom genre.

clue.text: Generated renown penning book for young child

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the letter goes inside
generated means produced, so the letters are reformed in a new order

explanation.surface: Fame produced by writing a children's book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generated' rearranges RENOWN; 'penning' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn is a baby just delivered, the youngest kind of child.

clue.text: One senior blocking obstinate person's bad government

indicators.note: blocking means obstructing from within, so these letters sit inside

parts.note: a mule is a stubborn person; the 's stands for is
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An elderly official obstructs a stubborn person's poor administration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' puts ISR inside MULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Misrule is incompetent or unjust governing of a state.

clue.text: Calculating people being slippery beasts

explanation.surface: Scheming people are snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both those who sum numbers and venomous European snakes.

clue.text: Use needle on covers at home connecting material

indicators.note: covers means encloses, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to sew is to use a needle and thread
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone does needlework on cushion covers at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' is a verb here: the stitching word encloses the home word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinew is a tendon, tissue joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Bugs from opposing directions constricting chest

indicators.note: constricting means squeezing around, so the chest sits inside

parts.note: N and S, north and south, are opposite compass points
an ark is a chest or box

explanation.surface: Insects coming from both sides tighten round someone's ribcage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constricting' puts ARK between N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To nark someone is British slang to annoy or irritate them, as bugs does.

clue.text: Ill-favoured outskirts of Dundee abandoned by father and daughter

indicators.note: the outskirts are the outer letters of the word, which go
abandoned says those outer letters are dropped, keeping the inside

parts.note: a sire is a father

explanation.surface: An unattractive town's edges are deserted by a parent and child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of … abandoned' strips D and E from Dundee, a Scottish city, to leave UNDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-favoured means unwanted or not in favour, someone no one desires.

clue.text: Spoil preserve adding in yellow herb

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: adding in means putting something into the middle of another

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
or is the heraldic gold or yellow

explanation.surface: Ruining a jar of jam by stirring in a yellow herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adding in' places the heraldic colour inside the preserve, after the spoiling word.
explanation.definitionFit: Marjoram is an aromatic plant of the mint family used in cooking.

clue.text: Ending fast early, that man gets pastry product

indicators.note: with 'early', the word's ending is cut short
ending early means stopping before the last letter

parts.note: quick means fast
he is that man

explanation.surface: A man breaks his fast early and gets a savoury tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ending … early' drops the last letter of QUICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiche is a savoury open tart with an egg filling in a pastry case.

clue.text: Sins circulated with one's tendency to pry

indicators.note: circulated means sent round, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters ONES

explanation.surface: Gossip spreads about someone's misdeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulated' mixes SINS and ONES together.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosiness is an inquisitive interest in other people's business.

clue.text: Against South American cleric returning

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: US means American
Rev, Reverend, is a cleric's title

explanation.surface: A South American priest comes home in opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses SUSREV.
explanation.definitionFit: Versus means in opposition to, as in a match between two teams.
